title: Pre-Commit Hooks
description: Write pre-commit hooks that run linters, formatters, and fast checks before code enters the repository.

data.text: The pre-commit hook runs after you type git commit but before the commit is created. It is the primary gate for ensuring code quality at commit time. Good pre-commit hooks run fast checks that catch issues in seconds, not minutes.

items: Run linters (ESLint, ShellCheck, dotnet format, etc.)
Validate file naming and structure conventions
Run fast unit tests for changed files only
Prevent committing files that should be ignored

data.title: Keep pre-commit fast
data.text: Pre-commit hooks block the commit command. If they take more than a few seconds, developers will bypass them with --no-verify. Move expensive checks to pre-push or CI.
Pre-commit hooks receive no arguments but can access the staged files via git diff --cached --name-only. Use this to run checks only on files that are being committed, not the entire repository.

data.title: Pre-commit hook: lint only staged files
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# .git/hooks/pre-commit

# Get list of staged files
STAGED_FILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM)

if [ -z "$STAGED_FILES" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Run ESLint only on staged JS/TS files
echo "Running ESLint on staged files..."
npx eslint $STAGED_FILES --ext .js,.ts,.tsx
ESLINT_EXIT=$?

if [ $ESLINT_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "ESLint failed. Fix errors before committing."
  exit 1
fi

echo "Lint passed."
exit 0

data.text: Pre-commit is the ideal place to prevent secrets from entering the repository. Tools like gitleaks and git-secrets scan staged files for common secret patterns (API keys, passwords, private keys) and block the commit if found.

data.title: Pre-commit secret scanning with gitleaks
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# .git/hooks/pre-commit

# Run gitleaks on staged files
gitleaks protect --staged --verbose --redact
GITLEAKS_EXIT=$?

if [ $GITLEAKS_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "Potential secrets detected in staged files!"
  echo "Remove them or use git commit --no-verify to skip."
  exit 1
fi

echo "No secrets detected."
exit 0

data.text: Husky is a popular tool that makes Git hooks easy to manage in Node.js projects. It installs hooks from .husky/ in your repository, which is committed to Git. This solves the 'hooks are local' problem.

data.title: Set up a pre-commit hook with Husky
data.code:
# Install Husky
npm install --save-dev husky
npx husky init

# Create the pre-commit hook
npx husky add .husky/pre-commit "npx lint-staged"

# Configure lint-staged in package.json
# {
#   "lint-staged": {
#     "*.{ts,tsx}": ["eslint --fix", "git add"]
#   }
# }

# Commit the .husky/ directory
git add .husky/
git commit -m "chore: add Husky pre-commit hook"

items.question: Can pre-commit modify staged files?
items.answer: Yes. Hooks can modify files, but you must stage the changes before the hook exits. Tools like Husky and lint-staged handle this automatically by running git add after fixes.

items.question: What happens if the hook takes too long?
items.answer: Git waits until the hook exits. If it hangs, the terminal appears frozen. You can kill it with Ctrl+C and then use git commit --no-verify to bypass it.

items.question: Can I skip a pre-commit hook?
items.answer: Yes, with git commit --no-verify. This should be rare and for emergency cases only, not a daily habit.

items.question: Does pre-commit run on amend?
items.answer: Yes. git commit --amend triggers pre-commit just like a normal commit. The hook can access the staged files normally.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: pre-commit runs before the commit is created — use it for fast quality checks
Access staged files with git diff --cached --name-only
Keep hooks fast — slow hooks get bypassed with --no-verify
Use gitleaks or git-secrets to prevent secrets from being committed
Use Husky to share hooks across your team via committed .husky/ files
